progressionInfo.name: I-vi-IV-V Progression
progressionInfo.subtitle: The iconic four-chord cycle that defined 1950s doo-wop and continues to power emotional ballads and pop songs across every era.

properties.label: I (Tonic)
properties.value: Stability, home base, point of departure

properties.label: vi (Submediant)
properties.value: Relative minor, adds melancholy and emotional depth

properties.label: IV (Subdominant)
properties.value: Movement and tension, pulls away from home

properties.label: V (Dominant)
properties.value: Maximum yearning, demands resolution back to I

chordDiagrams.description: Open position chords for the classic doo-wop sound:
practiceNotes: The Am shares two notes with C major (C and E)

advancedApplications.title: Common Variations
advancedApplications.description: Ways the doo-wop progression is modified:
items: I-vi-ii-V (replace IV with ii for jazz flavor)
I-vi-IV-V7 (add seventh to dominant for stronger pull)
I-vi-IV-V-I-vi-ii-V (8-bar extended version)
vi-IV-I-V (start on vi for modern pop feel)
I-vi-IV-V with bass walkdowns between chords

advancedApplications.title: Rhythm Patterns
items: Doo-wop triplet feel: boom-ba-da boom-ba-da
Slow ballad: whole note arpeggios
50s shuffle: swing eighth notes
Modern pop: steady eighth note strumming
Fingerpicking: Travis picking pattern

advancedApplications.title: Key Transpositions
items: C Major: C - Am - F - G
G Major: G - Em - C - D
D Major: D - Bm - G - A
E Major: E - C#m - A - B
F Major: F - Dm - Bb - C

sections.title: Scale Degrees in C Major
items: I (C): 1st degree - Tonic
vi (Am): 6th degree - Relative minor
IV (F): 4th degree - Subdominant
V (G): 5th degree - Dominant
All four chords are diatonic to C major

sections.title: Shared Notes Between Chords
items: C (C-E-G) and Am (A-C-E) share C and E
Am (A-C-E) and F (F-A-C) share A and C
F (F-A-C) and G (G-B-D) share no notes
This note sharing creates smooth voice leading

sections.title: Why It Works
items: I and vi are closely related (relative major/minor)
Moving to vi introduces minor quality (sadness)
IV creates forward motion away from home
V creates maximum tension for resolution back to I
The cycle creates a complete emotional journey

sections.title: Scales for Soloing
items: C major pentatonic works over entire progression
A minor pentatonic for bluesy soloing
Target chord tones on each change
Use the full C major scale for melodic playing
